unit: One original question, plus each required reference point as an unweighted unit.
complete: All required points appear accurately in the published answer; all material published claims are source-supported by their citations, and all required caveats and limitations are preserved with correct scope.
partial: At least one required point accurately published, but the complete criteria are unmet. Unsupported claims are independently counted even in a partial answer.
false_abstention: No factual findings published even though the actual synthesis packet jointly supports all required points. An abstention from a packet that supports only some points is reported separately. Execution errors are never scored as abstentions.
citation_support: Check exact ID and verbatim quote first; independently check that the source entails the precise claim including metric, unit, method, population, table row/header, configuration and scope. Count supported, unsupported, and unreviewed published claims with denominators. Review cited limitations separately.
point_attribution: If a sufficient source set never appears in any effective packet, identify missing retrieval versus selection using matching search-return IDs and synthesis packet IDs. Without per-candidate rank or index evidence, leave the substage unresolved. Accept independently checked equivalent anchors and document them without editing frozen references.
If a packet supplied the answer but the draft omitted the point, label draft omission. If the draft misstated it, label wrong or unsupported draft. Keep missing and incorrect claims distinct.

When the same round contains sufficient evidence and a correct draft that was held, label verification hold only if the recorded verdict/check shows it. If a verified claim disappeared during round selection, label publication loss. Track each round separately and score completeness only on the final envelope.
If no answer can be scored because of a provider or execution error, report the error stage. Do not infer answer incorrectness or assign an unsupported-claim count to missing output.
review_status: References source-checked by the preparing assistant. Live scoring is machine-assisted unless an independent human reviewer signs off. Disputes are inconclusive and are never resolved by editing the frozen expected points.
usage: Report wall time per question plus median and p90 across completed attempts, per-search and per-stage timings, CLI invocations including failures, and receipt token counts where present. No estimate of internal HTTP retries.
completion: Publish counts and denominators for successful, partial, false-abstention, evidence-limited, unsupported, inconclusive, execution-error and unrun cases. Identify the most frequent confirmed earliest failure only if the observed counts support it.
